results.label: Theorem 2.1 (Square-root minimax rate).
results.statement:
[S2.Thmtheorem1] Theorem 2.1 (Square-root minimax rate).
 [S2.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
For every integer  $T\geq 2$ ,
 [S2.EGx1] 
 $\displaystyle\frac{1}{4320}\sqrt{T}$  $\displaystyle\leq V_{T}^{\mathrm{rand,ad}}\leq U_{T}<\sqrt{T},$ (2.7)

 $\displaystyle\frac{1}{1200}\sqrt{T}$  $\displaystyle\leq V_{T}^{\mathrm{det,obl}}\leq U_{T}<\sqrt{T}.$ (2.8)

An integer minimizer in (2.6) is
 [S2.E9] 
 $m_{T}^{*}=\left\lceil\frac{\sqrt{4T+1}-1}{2}\right\rceil.$ (2.9)

For  $T=1$ , both minimax values equal  $1/2$ .

results.label: Corollary 2.2 (Horizon-free guarantee).
results.statement:
[S2.Thmtheorem2] Corollary 2.2 (Horizon-free guarantee).
 [S2.Thmtheorem2.p1] 
There is a single deterministic forecaster, independent of the terminal horizon, such that for every infinite outcome sequence and every prefix  $T\geq 1$ ,
 [S2.E10] 
 $\operatorname{CalDist}(p_{1:T},y_{1:T})<(2+\sqrt{2})\sqrt{T}.$ (2.10)

In the word-RAM model of Proposition 6.5, with word size  $\Omega(\log(T+1))$ , it uses  $O(\log(T+1))$  time per round and  $O(\sqrt{T})$  memory at time  $T$ .

results.label: Remark 2.3 (The remaining quantifier order).
results.statement:
[S2.Thmtheorem3] Remark 2.3 (The remaining quantifier order).
 [S2.Thmtheorem3.p1] 
For a randomized forecaster against a fixed string, define
 [S2.Ex6] 
 $V_{T}^{\mathrm{rand,obl}}:=\inf_{K}\sup_{y\in\{0,1\}^{T}}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\operatorname{CalDist}(P^{K}(y),y)\right].$ 

Fix jointly Borel sampling maps that realize the kernels by inverse transforms, and let  $W=(W_{1},\ldots,W_{T})$  have independent  $\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]$  coordinates. For each fixed  $w$ , let  $F^{w}$  be the resulting deterministic rule and set  $L(w,y):=\operatorname{CalDist}(p^{F^{w}}(y),y)$ . The deterministic result bounds  $\mathbb{E}_{W}[\sup_{y}L(W,y)]$ . The displayed value instead requires control of  $\sup_{y}\mathbb{E}_{W}[L(W,y)]$ , and these two operations cannot be exchanged in this direction. Conversely, the adversary for (2.7) depends on past realized forecasts and is not a fixed string. Thus  $V_{T}^{\mathrm{rand,obl}}$  remains open.

results.label: Lemma 4.1 (Witness comparison).
results.statement:
[S4.Thmtheorem1] Lemma 4.1 (Witness comparison).
 [S4.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
For every integer  $T\geq 1$ ,  $p\in[0,1]^{T}$ ,  $y\in\{0,1\}^{T}$ , and Lipschitz  $f:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}$ , let  $L:=\operatorname{Lip}(f)$  be its least Lipschitz constant and  $B:=\left\lVert f\right\rVert_{\infty}$ . Then
 [S4.E1] 
 $\left\lvert\sum_{t=1}^{T}f(p_{t})(y_{t}-p_{t})\right\rvert\leq(L+B)\operatorname{CalDist}(p,y).$ (4.1)

Consequently,
 [S4.EGx2] 
 $\displaystyle\operatorname{CalDist}(p,y)$  $\displaystyle\geq\left\lvert\sum_{t=1}^{T}(y_{t}-p_{t})\right\rvert,$ (4.2)

 $\displaystyle\operatorname{CalDist}(p,y)$  $\displaystyle\geq\frac{2}{3}\left\lvert\sum_{t=1}^{T}(1/2-p_{t})(y_{t}-p_{t})\right\rvert.$ (4.3)

results.label: Theorem 5.1 (Randomized simultaneous lower bound).
results.statement:
[S5.Thmtheorem1] Theorem 5.1 (Randomized simultaneous lower bound).
 [S5.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
For every integer  $T\geq 2$  and every Borel behavioral-kernel forecaster  $K$  defined in Section 2, there is a Borel-measurable deterministic past-adaptive adversary  $A$  that does not observe the current forecast and satisfies
 [S5.E1] 
 $\mathbb{E}^{K,A}\operatorname{CalDist}(P,Y)\geq\frac{1}{4320}\sqrt{T}.$ (5.1)

results.label: Theorem 5.2 (Deterministic oblivious lower bound).
results.statement:
[S5.Thmtheorem2] Theorem 5.2 (Deterministic oblivious lower bound).
 [S5.Thmtheorem2.p1] 
For every integer  $T\geq 2$  and deterministic nonanticipating forecaster  $F$ , there is a fixed string  $y\in\{0,1\}^{T}$  such that
 [S5.E18] 
 $\operatorname{CalDist}\bigl(p^{F}(y),y\bigr)\geq\frac{1}{1200}\sqrt{T}.$ (5.18)

results.label: Lemma 6.1 (Shifted-bias invariant).
results.statement:
[S6.Thmtheorem1] Lemma 6.1 (Shifted-bias invariant).
 [S6.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
Under the construction (6.1)–(6.4), for every  $t\in\{0,\ldots,T\}$  and  $j\in\{0,\ldots,m\}$ ,
 [S6.E6] 
 $x_{j}-1\leq\beta_{t,j}\leq x_{j},\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad-\frac{1}{2}\leq b_{t,j}\leq\frac{1}{2}.$ (6.6)

results.label: Lemma 6.2 (Proxy comparison).
results.statement:
[S6.Thmtheorem2] Lemma 6.2 (Proxy comparison).
 [S6.Thmtheorem2.p1] 
For every integer  $T\geq 1$ ,  $u,p\in[0,1]^{T}$ , and  $y\in\{0,1\}^{T}$ ,
 [S6.EGx8] 
 $\displaystyle\left\lvert\operatorname{CalDist}(p,y)-\operatorname{CalDist}(u,y)\right\rvert$  $\displaystyle\leq\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left\lvert p_{t}-u_{t}\right\rvert,$ (6.7)

 $\displaystyle\operatorname{CalDist}(p,y)$  $\displaystyle\leq\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left\lvert p_{t}-u_{t}\right\rvert+\operatorname{ECE}(u,y).$ (6.8)

results.label: Proposition 6.3 (Finite-horizon pathwise bound).
results.statement:
[S6.Thmtheorem3] Proposition 6.3 (Finite-horizon pathwise bound).
 [S6.Thmtheorem3.p1] 
For every integer  $T\geq 1$  and  $m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ , the construction (6.1)–(6.4) satisfies, on every outcome sequence,
 [S6.E9] 
 $\operatorname{CalDist}(p,y)\leq g_{T}(m)=\frac{T}{2m}+\frac{m-1}{2}.$ (6.9)

results.label: Corollary 6.4 (Exact grid optimization).
results.statement:
[S6.Thmtheorem4] Corollary 6.4 (Exact grid optimization).
 [S6.Thmtheorem4.p1] 
For every integer  $T\geq 1$ , the integer  $m_{T}^{*}$  in (2.9) minimizes  $g_{T}$ . Let  $\bar{m}:=\lceil\sqrt{T}\rceil$  and  $\delta:=\bar{m}-\sqrt{T}\in[0,1)$ . Then
 [S6.E10] 
 $U_{T}\leq g_{T}(\bar{m})=\sqrt{T}-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\delta^{2}}{2\bar{m}}<\sqrt{T}.$ (6.10)

results.label: Proposition 6.5 (Efficient exact implementation).
results.statement:
[S6.Thmtheorem5] Proposition 6.5 (Efficient exact implementation).
 [S6.Thmtheorem5.p1] 
For a fixed  $m\geq 1$ , the algorithm in (6.1)–(6.4) admits  $O(m)$  initialization time and memory, followed by  $O(\log(m+1))$  worst-case time per round. Its forecasts are represented exactly as rationals. All stored integers have  $O(\log(m+1))$  bits, so these bounds hold in a word-RAM with word size  $\Omega(\log(m+1))$ .

results.label: Lemma 7.1 (Block subadditivity).
results.statement:
[S7.Thmtheorem1] Lemma 7.1 (Block subadditivity).
 [S7.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
For every integer  $T\geq 1$ ,  $p\in[0,1]^{T}$ , and  $y\in\{0,1\}^{T}$ , let  $I_{1},\ldots,I_{K}$  be a partition of  $\{1,\ldots,T\}$  into nonempty consecutive blocks. Then
 [S7.E1] 
 $\operatorname{CalDist}(p,y)\leq\sum_{k=1}^{K}\operatorname{CalDist}(p_{I_{k}},y_{I_{k}}).$ (7.1)

additional_own_claims.scope: Finite public-history kernel products, no current forecast in adversary input, actual Borel bounded CalDist.
Own finite ECE opposite-outcome identity and T/2 lower, including causal fixed-string realization.
Actual smooth-witness supremum comparison, proved from own witness inequality.
Actual Hoeffding/product mgf iteration, exact tail integration and fourth moments, cubic interpolation, Holder/Jensen drift, logarithmic exponent and exact constants.

model_boundaries.finite_horizon_encoding: Behavioral strategies are encoded on all n; each T law reads only its first T transitions. A finite-horizon family may extend by an arbitrary constant probability kernel after T, without restricting any source strategy. Strategies at each T can depend on T.
model_boundaries.word_ram: Source unit-cost word arithmetic/record access and continuation/root-handle model. Formal exact quantities are record visits, word widths, actual suspended-job work/deadline and arena footprints. No compiler/GC wall-clock theorem is asserted.
model_boundaries.implementation_variant: Cached complete binary trees implement the same grid choices and forecasts; no unformalized balanced-tree complexity theorem is assumed.
model_boundaries.randomized_oblivious: No square-root randomized-oblivious lower bound is claimed.
